# Project Control Systems



::: {.callout-note}
This chapter is in preparation. The MGMT-3105 course map lists a *Control
Systems* lecture in this slot; the chapter will be built from project-control
fundamentals and the course's Project Manager Report and Team Member Report
templates, following the same structure as [Chapter 1](01-Sustainability.qmd)
and [Chapter 9](09-Cost-Estimation-and-Budgeting.qmd).
:::

## Learning objectives (planned)

By the end of this chapter you will be able to:

- Describe the monitoring-and-control loop: measure, compare to baseline, analyse variance, act.
- Compute earned-value metrics: PV, EV, AC, SV, CV, SPI, CPI.
- Forecast with EAC, ETC, and TCPI, and interpret the results.
- Build and read an S-curve of planned vs. earned vs. actual cost.
- Run integrated change control and keep the baseline meaningful.
- Report status honestly: the "watermelon" trap and leading vs. lagging indicators.

## Topic outline

1. What "control" means: closed-loop management.
2. The performance measurement baseline (scope + schedule + cost).
3. Earned value management: the three curves and the six core metrics.
4. Variance analysis and forecasting (EAC scenarios, TCPI).
5. Change control and configuration management.
6. Status reporting, dashboards, and honest metrics.
7. Running case: an earned-value snapshot of the RC-vehicle project at week 8.
